_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Gabon covering early Bantu and Pygmy peoples, Fang migration, Orungu and Mpongwe coastal trading states, French colonisation, Albert Schweitzer at Lambaréné, the Bongo dynasty (Omar 42 years, Ali 14 years), oil wealth, and the 2023 coup ending the Bongo dynasty.

ethnic_groups.name: Fang
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu; northern and central Gabon; largest single group; Woleu-Ntem, Ogooué-Ivindo provinces

ethnic_groups.name: Mpongwe
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal Bantu; Libreville area; historically dominant in trade with Europeans; first largely urban group

ethnic_groups.name: Nzebi/Bandzabi
ethnic_groups.notes: South-central; Ngounié province; part of larger Teke-Mbete cultural zone

ethnic_groups.name: Mbede
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Gabon; Haut-Ogooué; related to broader Teke peoples

ethnic_groups.name: Punu
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Gabon; Ngounié province; known for white-faced Okuyi masks

ethnic_groups.name: Teke
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern plateau; cross-border with Congo-Brazzaville; Teke kingdom heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Myene/Orungu
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal cluster including Orungu, Galwa, Enenga; historical middlemen in slave trade

ethnic_groups.name: Kota
ethnic_groups.notes: Northeast; Ogooué-Ivindo; famous for brass-covered reliquary figures

ethnic_groups.name: Pygmy (Baka, Babongo, Bakoya)
ethnic_groups.notes: Forest hunter-gatherers; among oldest inhabitants; marginalized communities

ethnic_groups.name: Other (including European/Lebanese)
ethnic_groups.notes: French expatriates, Lebanese traders, other African migrants

natural_resources.notes: Oil backbone of economy since 1960s; world's #2 manganese producer (after South Africa, Moanda mine largest globally); timber exports (okoumé wood); Bélinga iron ore (massive deposit, Chinese interest, environmental controversy); 88% forest cover (one of most forested globally)

military.notes: August 2023 military coup ended Bongo dynasty (55 years, Ali Bongo ousted); General Brice Oligui Nguema transitional leader; French military presence (largest base in Gulf of Guinea); small but equipped forces; Republican Guard historically protected Bongo family

climate_environment.notes: 13 national parks created 2002 (one of Africa's most ambitious conservation programs); 88% forest cover; carbon-positive country; Lopé National Park UNESCO; rainforest elephants, gorillas

debt_aid.notes: Oil wealth created upper-middle-income status but benefits concentrated; Bongo family wealth estimated $1B+; IMF Extended Fund Facility; post-coup transition government reforming

education.notes: French-language instruction; free public education; relatively well-funded compared to region; students also study in France/Morocco; small population means limited scale; oil wealth enabled significant education investment

diaspora_migration.notes: Small diaspora relative to oil wealth; French connections strong; immigration hub (workers from Cameroon, Congo, West Africa); Albert Schweitzer hospital legacy at Lambaréné drew international attention

digital_economy.notes: Relatively high internet penetration for Central Africa; submarine cables (SAT3/WASC/ACE); oil sector IT spending significant; limited startup ecosystem; e-government improving post-coup reforms

country_profile.notes_unique: Over 80% of the country is covered by tropical rainforest; the Lopé-Okanda landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site blending dense forest and savanna.

current_leader.name: Brice Oligui Nguema
current_leader.title: Transitional President
current_leader.notes: Led military coup deposing Ali Bongo; cousin of the Bongo family; promised democratic transition

prime_minister.name: Raymond Ndong Sima
prime_minister.notes: Former opposition leader; previously PM under Omar Bongo 2012–2014

former_leaders.name: Léon M'ba
former_leaders.notes: First president; Fang leader; restored by French military after 1964 coup

former_leaders.name: Omar Bongo Ondimba
former_leaders.notes: 42 years in power; world's longest-serving president at death; converted to Islam; renamed country 'Gabonese Republic'; oil wealth and La Françafrique ties

former_leaders.name: Ali Bongo Ondimba
former_leaders.notes: Son of Omar; disputed elections 2009, 2016, 2023; health crisis 2018–2019; deposed by military August 2023

910.name: Early Peoples and Forest Settlement
910.description: BaKa and other Pygmy hunter-gatherers inhabit the equatorial rainforest; early Bantu-speaking farmers arrive bringing iron smelting and agriculture.

sub_clusters.name: BaKa and Pygmy Forest Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Indigenous hunter-gatherer communities in Gabon's dense equatorial rainforest; among the earliest inhabitants of the region.

sub_clusters.name: Early Bantu Settlement and Ironworking
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking farmers migrate into Gabon; ironworking sites in the Ogooué River valley; gradual forest clearance for agriculture.

910.name: Okanda and Ancient Iron Sites
910.description: Ancient iron-smelting sites in the Lopé-Okanda region represent some of the earliest metallurgy in Central Africa; UNESCO World Heritage landscapes.

sub_clusters.name: Lopé-Okanda Iron Age Sites
sub_clusters.description: Extensive iron-smelting remains in the Lopé National Park area; rock engravings; evidence of early forest-savanna boundary management by human communities.

920.name: Fang Migration into Gabon
920.description: The Fang people migrate southward from Cameroon and become Gabon's largest ethnic group; warrior culture, Bieri ancestor worship, and forest adaptation.

sub_clusters.name: Fang Southward Movement
sub_clusters.description: Fang clans push through the equatorial forest; absorb or displace earlier Bantu groups; establish villages along river corridors; segmentary lineage system.

sub_clusters.name: Fang Art and Bieri Tradition
sub_clusters.description: Fang create renowned Bieri reliquary figures; elaborate initiation ceremonies; rich oral traditions; artistic heritage later prized by European modernists.

920.name: Mpongwe and Orungu Coastal Trading States
920.description: Mpongwe and Orungu peoples dominate the Gabon Estuary and Ogooué Delta; middlemen in slave, ivory, and dyewood trade with Europeans.

sub_clusters.name: Mpongwe Trade at the Gabon Estuary
sub_clusters.description: Mpongwe clans control trade at the Gabon Estuary (Libreville area); intermediaries between European ships and interior peoples; accumulate wealth and adopt some European customs.

sub_clusters.name: Orungu Kingdom of the Ogooué Delta
sub_clusters.description: Orungu kings dominate the Ogooué River delta and Cape Lopez; major slave-exporting polity; negotiate with Dutch, French, and British traders.

930.name: Slave Trade and French Establishment
930.description: Portuguese reach the Gabon Estuary 1472; slave and ivory trade dominated by European companies; France establishes control through treaties with Mpongwe chiefs.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Contact and Early Trade
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese traders name the Gabon estuary (from 'gabão', a hooded cloak); trade in slaves, ivory, and redwood with coastal peoples.

sub_clusters.name: French Treaties and Founding of Libreville
sub_clusters.description: Captain Bouët-Willaumez signs treaties with Mpongwe chiefs 1839; French naval base established; freed slaves settle at Libreville ('Free Town') 1849.

940.name: French Colonial Gabon (1880–1960)
940.description: Gabon becomes part of French Equatorial Africa; Brazza explores the Ogooué; concessionary companies, timber exploitation, and Albert Schweitzer's hospital.

sub_clusters.name: Brazza's Ogooué Expeditions
sub_clusters.description: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza ascends the Ogooué River; establishes French claims in the interior; treaties with Fang and other chiefs.

sub_clusters.name: Concessionary Companies and Timber
sub_clusters.description: Concessionary companies exploit rubber and ivory; after 1920 timber (okoumé) becomes principal export; forced labour for logging and porterage.

sub_clusters.name: Albert Schweitzer at Lambaréné
sub_clusters.description: Alsatian physician-theologian Albert Schweitzer founds hospital at Lambaréné 1913; Nobel Peace Prize 1952; controversial paternalism but globally famous humanitarian symbol.

950.name: Independence and Léon Mba
950.description: Léon Mba leads Gabon to independence; one-party rule; 1964 coup attempt reversed by French military intervention; Mba grooms Omar Bongo.

sub_clusters.name: Gabon Independence
sub_clusters.description: Gabon independent 17 August 1960 under Léon Mba; BDG single-party rule; close ties with France; manganese and uranium mining begins.

sub_clusters.name: 1964 Coup and French Intervention
sub_clusters.description: Military coup briefly deposes Mba; French paratroopers restore him within 24 hours under defence agreements; first French military intervention in post-colonial Africa.

950.name: Omar Bongo Dynasty (1967–2009)
950.description: Omar Bongo (later El Hadj Omar Bongo Ondimba) rules for 42 years; oil wealth funds patronage; master of Françafrique diplomacy; multiparty reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Omar Bongo's Rise and Oil Boom
sub_clusters.description: Albert-Bernard Bongo becomes president at 31; oil production booms from 1970s; single-party PDG state; converts to Islam 1973; renames to El Hadj Omar Bongo.

sub_clusters.name: Multiparty Transition and Continued Rule
sub_clusters.description: Prodemocracy protests and Port-Gentil riots 1990; national conference; multiparty elections but Bongo wins each time; dies in office June 2009 after 42 years.

960.name: Ali Bongo Ondimba and the 2023 Coup
960.description: Ali Bongo succeeds his father; disputed elections; stroke 2018; military coup August 2023 ends the Bongo dynasty after 56 years.

sub_clusters.name: Ali Bongo Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Ali Bongo wins contested election 2009 (Port-Gentil riots); re-elected 2016 amid violent post-election crisis; suffers stroke 2018; questions about fitness to govern.

sub_clusters.name: 2023 Military Coup
sub_clusters.description: Military officers led by General Brice Oligui Nguema overthrow Ali Bongo minutes after disputed election results announced August 2023; ends 56-year Bongo dynasty; transition government.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Economy and Diversification Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Oil dominates Gabonese economy since the 1970s; declining production since peak in 1997; efforts to diversify into mining (manganese), timber, and ecotourism; deep inequality persists.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
